subject: Audit log exportability & evidence pack — post-discovery action items
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Brooks <emma.brooks@healthlake.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Audit log exportability & evidence pack — post-discovery action items

Emma — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on deliverables and timing:

Summary of what we discussed:
- Inventory: You need admin activity logs (user role changes, console/API admin actions), API request/response logs (inbound requests, model id, request metadata), and system events (node restarts, scaling events).
- Exportability: HealthLake wants a self-serve export (CSV/JSON) for a bounded time range, plus an option for periodic S3 exports.
- Immutability/Retention: Two asks — (A) WORM-style retention for audit exports for 12 months, and (B) signed export artifacts for forensic chain-of-custody is desirable.
- Compliance evidence: SOC 2 report and CSV/JSON samples of the export schema to validate ingestion.

Proposed action items (what Redwood will deliver):
1) Sample export schema + 48-hour proof-of-concept export to the Drive folder we agreed to. (Deliverable: auditlog_sample_schema.csv) — target: 2026-08-20 EOD.
2) High-level immutability options doc (what we can support today: S3 write-once + signed checksums; longer-term: hardware-backed WORM) — target: 2026-08-24.
3) SOC 2 artifact pointer (we can provide the SOC 2 type II overview and the auditor name; redacted reports via secure link) — target: 2026-08-20.
4) Vendor security questionnaire completion: we can start with the exported logs sample and SOC pointer; please send the XLSX if you want us to fill it in.

Can you confirm that timeline works and whether you prefer the sample export as CSV or newline-delimited JSON? I’ll loop in Priyom for the export mechanics and Marissa for compliance packaging.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: auditlog_sample_schema.csv (stub)

From: Emma Brooks <emma.brooks@healthlake.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthLake Security <security@healthlake.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit log exportability & evidence pack — post-discovery action items

Thanks Marcus — that recap is perfect. A few clarifications from my side (security):

- CSV is preferable for our initial ingestion pipeline, but NDJSON would also work if the records have stable keys. Please include an example event for: role_change, api_call, and node_event.
- For immutability: we need the export to include a signed checksum (SHA256) and a timestamp per file. S3 write-once (object lock) is fine.
- Vendor SQ: attaching the questionnaire we use internally. If you can pre-fill any sections about log collection and retention, that would speed review.

Timeline looks good. For the SOC 2 pointer, we only need the auditor name and whether Redwood is in-scope for logging controls (CC3/CC6 equivalents).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — I’ll review the sample exports when you drop them in the Drive link.

Best,
Emma Brooks
Security Manager, HealthLake
emma.brooks@healthlake.com

Attachment: vendor-security-questionnaire.xlsx (stub)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Audit log exportability & evidence pack — coordination

Marcus / Marissa — quick internal note on implementation:

- I’ll produce a sample CSV that includes minimal fields: timestamp_utc, event_type, user_id, actor_ip, request_id, model_id, request_meta (json-encoded), checksum. That should cover HealthLake’s initial asks.
- For signed checksums: we can provide SHA256 checksums and a detached signature (PEM) for each export using our current key. If HealthLake needs HSM-backed signatures, we can discuss roadmap but not in the initial POC.
- For the S3 write-once retention, we already support object lock & legal-hold features on our managed export buckets for Dedicated and Hosted customers — Marissa, can you prepare the compliance blurb for the SOC pointer?

I’ll aim to drop the CSV sample and the signature file into the Drive folder by 2026-08-20 16:00 PT.

— Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

3) Redwood: once you confirm, we’ll schedule a short tech call (30 minutes) to demo the export flow and S3 object-lock configuration.

If you prefer, I can schedule the demo for the week of Aug 24 — Marcus, please coordinate with Emma.

Thanks — Marissa
